title: Salary switchers drift away
disclaimer: Practice scenario. The company is fictional and every figure is hypothetical. Australian market context is general.
company_context: Brightbank (fictional) is an Australian app-only bank offering everyday accounts, savings and cards, and aims to become customers' main bank.

brief.problem: New customers who move their salary to Brightbank are moving it away again within six months.
brief.objective: Raise six-month salary retention from 58% to 75% within nine months.
baseline: Customers moving their salary in: about 4,000 a month.
Still salaried with us after six months: 58%, down from 72% a year ago.

facts.answer: A salaried customer earns us about $22 a month from interchange, deposit margin and fees. The 14-point drop means about 560 fewer salaried customers per monthly cohort — about $148k a year per cohort, and it compounds.
facts.coach_tip: Say the 'so what': main-bank customers are the whole business model.
facts.model_question: What's a salaried customer worth, and what does the drop cost?

facts.answer: Salary retention means the customer still receives at least one employer payment of $1,000 or more in month six after their first salary deposit.
facts.coach_tip: Now you know retention means salary staying, not the account staying open.

facts.answer: Under-30s: 61% retention (was 70%). 30–45s: 52% (was 74%). Customers with a home loan elsewhere: 41%.
facts.coach_tip: 30–45s and home-loan holders drop most — they have the most bills.
facts.model_question: Which customer segments are leaving most?

facts.answer: Before moving their salary out, leavers have only 1–2 bills or direct debits set up with us, compared with 6 or more for customers who stay. Most leavers never moved their direct debits across.
facts.coach_tip: Bills anchor customers — that's your lead.
facts.model_question: What do leavers do differently from customers who stay?

facts.answer: Switching journey: salary moved 100% → bill switch started 44% → bill switch completed 19% (was 47%).
facts.coach_tip: Completion fell from 47% to 19% — that's the break.
facts.model_question: Can I see the switching journey funnel?

facts.answer: Direct debit switching happens in the app. Customers must contact each biller themselves or enter biller details one by one.
facts.coach_tip: Manual effort per biller adds up fast.
facts.model_question: How do customers switch their bills today?

facts.answer: Eight months ago the automated 'switch my bills' service was turned off when the vendor contract ended. It was replaced with a manual checklist.
facts.coach_tip: Link this to the completion drop before calling it the cause.
facts.model_question: Did anything change in how customers switch their bills?

facts.answer: Exit survey: too hard to move everything 38%, better rate elsewhere 27%, missing features 21%, other 14%. App reviews mentioning switching tripled.
facts.coach_tip: Effort beats rate as the top reason.
facts.model_question: What do exit surveys and reviews say?

facts.answer: Our savings rate is 0.3 points below the top competitor and hasn't changed in 12 months.
facts.coach_tip: Unchanged for a year, so it doesn't explain the new drop.
facts.model_question: Could interest rates or competitors explain this?

facts.answer: Support gets about 2,600 contacts a month asking how to move direct debits.
facts.coach_tip: A cost-to-serve benefit and a guardrail.
facts.model_question: What's the support load from switching?

facts.answer: Estimates: better checklist with reminders — 2 weeks. Pre-filled switch list from the last 90 days of transactions, using Open Banking (CDR) consent — 6 weeks. PayTo-based bill switching for the top 50 billers — 10 weeks. Re-signing a switching vendor — 8 weeks plus $180k a year.
facts.coach_tip: Sort these into quick fix, medium and big bet.
facts.model_question: What are our options and estimates?

model_answer.problem_statement: Customers aged 30–45 who move their salary are leaving within six months because they never finish moving their bills — switch completion fell from 47% to 19% after the automated switching service was turned off — cutting salary retention from 72% to 58%, about 560 fewer salaried customers a month.

options.name: Checklist with reminders
options.description: Improve the checklist and nudge customers to finish.
options.business_impact: Small lift; cuts some support contacts.
options.why: Cheap, but still manual per biller.

options.name: Pre-filled switch list (CDR)
options.description: Use Open Banking consent to list every bill from 90 days of transactions, ready to switch.
options.customer_impact: See all your bills in one place, switch in a few taps.
options.business_impact: Targets the 38% 'too hard' reason; could recover most of the 560 a month.
options.why: Biggest effort reduction for the time.

options.name: PayTo bill switching
options.description: Move the top 50 billers to PayTo agreements automatically.
options.customer_impact: Bills move with almost no effort.
options.business_impact: Strongest long-term fix; slower to land.

model_answer.decision: Build the pre-filled switch list in 6 weeks, add reminders in 2 weeks as a quick win, and scope PayTo switching for next quarter.
model_answer.hypothesis: If we pre-fill each new customer's switch list from their last 90 days of transactions, bill switch completion will rise from 19% to 40% and six-month salary retention from 58% to 70% within two quarters, because leavers rarely move their direct debits and 38% say switching is too hard.
model_answer.test: A/B test new salaried customers: pre-filled switch list vs the current checklist for 8 weeks.
success_metrics: Direct debits per customer at day 60
guardrails: CDR consent rates and privacy complaints
